descriptions.Next.js 16: Organizes the pages and server services of Amará in one application. I used App Router and API routes to connect the interface with authentication, stored data, and the wellness assistant.
descriptions.React 19: Builds screens from reusable components. I used it to make both projects respond to user actions and changes in their data.
descriptions.TypeScript: Adds types to detect mistakes during development. I used it to define component data and communication contracts with the APIs in both projects.
descriptions.Tailwind CSS: Styles screens using consistent utilities. I used it to adapt the interfaces to different devices and keep forms, dashboards, and cards visually consistent.
descriptions.Tailwind CSS 4: Shapes the Amará interface using shared styling utilities and tokens. I used it to keep colors, spacing, and components consistent across mobile and desktop screens.
descriptions.Vite: Runs and builds the ObstetriCare frontend. I used it to develop the React and TypeScript interface and generate its distribution files.
descriptions.Recharts: Turns data into charts within React. I used it in ObstetriCare dashboards to present clinical information visually and make indicators and results easier to read.
descriptions.i18n: Makes one application available in multiple languages. In Amará, I organized Spanish and English text so users can switch languages without duplicating screens or their logic.
descriptions.FastAPI: Exposes the services connecting the ObstetriCare interface with its data and clinical logic. I used asynchronous endpoints to protect access and coordinate risk assessments.
descriptions.Python 3.12: Powers the ObstetriCare backend and its models. I used it to process clinical information, run the Machine Learning pipeline, and prepare reports for healthcare staff.
descriptions.SQLAlchemy 2.0 async: Connects code models to database tables. In ObstetriCare, I used it to query and save clinical information through asynchronous operations and transactions.
descriptions.asyncpg: Lets the backend communicate with PostgreSQL asynchronously. In ObstetriCare, I used it with SQLAlchemy to execute the API database operations.
descriptions.Alembic: Tracks changes to database tables. I used it in ObstetriCare to evolve the clinical schema through migrations rather than manually changing it in each environment.
descriptions.JWT: Identifies a user through a token after signing in. In ObstetriCare, I used it to authenticate API requests and apply permissions according to clinical staff roles.
descriptions.Supabase: Combines authentication, database, and storage services. In Amará, I used it to manage user sessions and store platform information with access controls.
descriptions.API Routes autenticadas: Server endpoints that check the session before handling a request. In Amará, I used them to protect sensitive operations and connect the assistant with the authenticated user context.
descriptions.PostgreSQL 16: Stores information in related tables for structured queries. In ObstetriCare, I used it to preserve patient records and the data required for clinical management.
descriptions.PostgreSQL: The relational database accessed through Supabase. In Amará, I used it to preserve emotional records, conversations, and other platform data associated with users.
descriptions.RLS: Applies permissions directly to table rows. In Amará, I used it with Supabase to restrict record access according to the authenticated user and protect personal information.
descriptions.Redis: Keeps temporary data in memory so it can be reused without repeating every query. In ObstetriCare, I used it as a cache to support queries and report preparation.
descriptions.Gemini 2.0 Flash: Generates content from the context it receives. I integrated it into ObstetriCare stage S-4 to produce clinical recommendation categories, with deterministic rules as a fallback if the service fails.
descriptions.OpenAI GPT-4o-mini: Powers the Amará conversational assistant. I integrated it to respond using recent emotional records and the available catalog as context while preserving user conversation history.
descriptions.Random Forest: Combines multiple decision trees for classification. I used it in ObstetriCare stage S-2 alongside other models to estimate preterm birth risk from ten clinical variables.
descriptions.CatBoost: Builds a classifier with progressively refined trees. In ObstetriCare stage S-2, I used it as part of the weighted consensus that combines different models to estimate risk.
descriptions.SVM: Classifies cases by finding a separation between groups of data. I used it with Random Forest and CatBoost in ObstetriCare S-2 to contribute another estimate to the preterm birth risk consensus.
descriptions.Regresión Logística Ordinal: Classifies outcomes that have an order, such as urgency levels. I used it in ObstetriCare S-3 with a decision tree and a weighted score to support triage classification.
descriptions.Árbol de Decisión: Classifies data through a sequence of decisions. I used it in ObstetriCare S-3 as part of the process assigning green, yellow, orange, or red urgency levels.
descriptions.Vercel: Publishes web applications at an accessible URL. I used it to deploy Amará and make its Next.js interface and server services available in the public demo.
descriptions.Migraciones SQL versionadas: Record database changes as code files. In Amará, I used them to keep the Supabase schema and its access policies evolving in a controlled way.
descriptions.YouTube API: Integrates YouTube content into an application. In Amará, I used it to include a player with music resources that accompany the wellness experience.
descriptions.WeasyPrint: Converts styled HTML documents into PDF files. In ObstetriCare, I used it to generate downloadable clinical reports formatted for reading and printing.
descriptions.OpenPyXL: Creates Excel files from Python. In ObstetriCare, I used it to export reports as spreadsheets so data can be reviewed outside the platform.
descriptions.pytest: Runs automated tests on Python code. In ObstetriCare, I used it to check critical services and detect regressions when changing the backend.

React 19.amara: I built components for the emotional calendar, statistics, and chat. React updates what users see when they record an emotion or interact with the assistant.
React 19.obstetricare: I built patient management screens and clinical dashboards from reusable components. React reflects clinical data and healthcare staff actions in the interface.

TypeScript.amara: I defined types for emotional records, components, and API route requests. This helps detect incompatible data before running the application.
TypeScript.obstetricare: I defined typed contracts for the clinical data exchanged between React and FastAPI. This makes forms and results easier to build around a consistent data structure.

Tailwind CSS.amara: I used Tailwind CSS 4 to give the calendar, chat, and wellness tools a consistent presentation. Its utilities adapt layouts to mobile and desktop screens.
Tailwind CSS.obstetricare: I styled forms, tables, and dashboards with shared utilities. This keeps the clinical interface consistent and lets each screen adapt to the available space.
